## Why it's sound (each adversarial axis verified against the worktree)

**Enforcement point is correct.** Two unrelated "editorial" surfaces exist; the spec gates the right one. The recap credit roll is assembled in `data.ts:332-354` from `event_vendors`, consumed only by `TeamBehindTheDay` (`editorial-content.tsx:106`, conditional on `data.vendors.length`; `:273` slices to 8). The 0038 blog/`/recommendations`/`affiliate_links` surface has no table/route substrate in this worktree — confirmed; deferring it is correct.

**The tier read reaches there (server, not client).** `data.ts` has no `'use client'` directive and uses `createAdminClient()` (service-role, RLS-bypassing). It is imported only by `editorial-content.tsx`, which is mounted by the **server** component `app/[slug]/page.tsx:706` (`export default async function PublicInvitationPage`). So the added `vendor_profiles.tier_state` probe runs server-side with admin privileges — it will read the column regardless of the anonymous visitor's (non-existent) RLS session. Correct.

**Substrate confirmed (not net-new):**
- `tier_state` exists — `supabase/migrations/20260714000000_v2_screen_name_reveal_mechanic.sql:70,102` (`CREATE TYPE vendor_tier_state`, `ADD COLUMN … NOT NULL DEFAULT 'free'`). It is excluded from `FULL_VENDOR_PROFILE_SELECT` (`vendor-profile.ts:86`), so the dedicated `.select('tier_state')` soft-probe is the established pattern (verbatim match to `branches/actions.ts:54-66`).
- Linkage `event_vendors.marketplace_vendor_id → vendor_profiles.vendor_profile_id` confirmed at `vendor-badges.ts:268-269`, `vendor-availability.ts:88-89`, and the marketplace-link writer `wizard-actions.ts:464`. The separate `event_vendors.vendor_id` PK exists and is correctly NOT used for the join.
- `editorialTagged` matrix confirmed: `free:false`/`verified:false`/`pro:true`/`enterprise:true` (`vendor-tier-caps.ts:86,108,130,152`); `tierCaps(null) → 'free' → false` via `asVendorTier`. Import alias `@/*` → `./*` resolves (`tsconfig.json:9`); `data.ts` already imports from `@/lib/*` at lines 17-18.

**Won't break couples/guests/other tiers.** `firstPickDen = rows.length` stays **before** the loop in the replacement, so M1 `servicesSetnayan`, M2 `firstPickDen`, M3 `hoursSaved` (data.ts:355,397,400-403) still count ALL rows. The spec correctly identifies the trap (gating the count would shrink the couple's headline stats) and avoids it. `VendorCredit[]` shape unchanged → no consumer/type break; empty array → section just doesn't render. Guests/other public widgets untouched.

**Failure mode is safe.** Probe miss / off-platform pick (`marketplace_vendor_id IS NULL`) → `tierById.get()` undefined → `tierCaps(undefined) → free → false` → excluded. Fail-open here means *fewer* credits, never over-grant.

## RLS / privacy — actually a net IMPROVEMENT, with one caveat to flag

The recap page is **public + anonymous + indexable** (`page.tsx:91,125,178` — "rendered for anonymous public visitors too, who have no RLS session"). The credit roll surfaces `event_vendors.vendor_name`, which is a **couple-typed snapshot** captured at lock time (`wizard-actions.ts:461,1106`), bypassing the entire hybrid-anonymity machinery (`name_revealed_at` reveal trigger + `screen_name` placeholders, `vendors.ts:309-424`). **Today, pre-gate, this credits ALL linked vendors by their snapshot name on a public page — including Free/Verified vendors whose marketplace name may still be hidden.** The gate *narrows* crediting to Pro/Enterprise only, whose `nameMode='true'` (names public day-1, `vendor-tier-caps.ts:123,145`) — so the gate **closes** a latent anonymity leak rather than opening one. Good.

Caveat to note (not a blocker): the gate keys on **live `tier_state`**, but `vendor_name` is a **historical snapshot**. If a vendor was Pro at lock time and later downgrades to Free, the gate will (correctly per the matrix) stop crediting them — but a Free vendor who was *never* Pro and whose name the couple happened to type in still wouldn't be credited (good). The only residual: a vendor who is Pro *now* but whose snapshot `vendor_name` differs from current `business_name` will be credited under the stale label. Harmless (it's the couple's own label for their own vendor), but worth one line in the PR.

## What I verified against `origin/main` (local main is 467+ commits stale — the spec's line numbers are accurate against `origin/main`, which is what I read)

**Confirmed correct in the spec:**
- `lib/vendor-tier-caps.ts` exists; `reviewStarsCounted`/`reviewCommentsViewable` are defined per-tier exactly as stated (free=false/false · verified=true/false · pro=true/true · enterprise=true/true), and `git grep` confirms **zero non-definition references** — they are wired into the type but unused by any surface. The gate is genuinely "wire an existing field into existing renders." Not net-new.
- `asVendorTier`/`tierCaps` exist and behave as described (default-to-`'free'` on absence = conservative). Not net-new.
- The Phase B soft-probe pattern is real (`vendor-dashboard/profile/page.tsx` ~l.194-201). The spec's probe approach matches shipped precedent.
- **Microsite** (`app/v/[slug]/page.tsx`, 1486 lines, server component): every line ref is accurate — `fetchVendor` `fullSelect`/`legacySelect` + fallback regex (~l.197/208), aggregateRating gate (l.556), `ReviewsSection` call (l.969)/def (l.1190), `ReviewHeroMetrics` (l.1218), `ReviewRow` (l.1300), `StarRow` (l.1315), `review.body` (l.1322), `AxisStat` (l.1326-1329), `vendor_reply` (l.1331). All gate points land on real code.
- **Marketplace** (`app/vendors/page.tsx`): batched `vendor_profiles` select at l.1427, `meta` enrichment at l.1527, `computeVendorBadges` at l.1550-1556, `<VendorCard>` props at l.1800-1803. All accurate.
- **Compare** (`app/vendors/compare/page.tsx`): `CompareRow` type l.42, `vendor_profiles` admin select l.138, Rating cell l.411-441, `'new'` fallback l.432. Accurate.
- **Server-vs-client / tier-read-reaches-there:** YES for all three. All three are server components reading via the **service-role `admin` client** (microsite `fetchVendor`, marketplace main query, compare query all use `admin` because anonymous viewers hit these and `vendor_profiles` is RLS-gated). So `tier_state` is readable and the gate decision is made server-side before render — a client cannot strip it. Correct.
- **Couples/guests/other-tier impact:** none. The gate only suppresses display for FREE/VERIFIED reviewed-vendors; it never touches the viewer's identity. Verified+ stars and Pro+ comments are unaffected. `tier_state` absent → `'free'` → most-restrictive, which is safe. The SCOPE-OUT of `vendor-dashboard/reviews/page.tsx` (self-view) is correct and necessary — gating in the lib (`fetchReviewStatsForMany`/`fetchLatestReviewsByVendor`) WOULD break the self-view since those same libs feed the dashboard; keeping the gate at the surface layer is the right call.

## The fix the spec is missing (this is why it's needs-fix, not sound)

**Ranking leak — the marketplace SORTS by hidden stars.** `app/vendors/page.tsx` l.1156-1176 issues the main query against the **`vendor_market_stats` VIEW** and orders by `avg_rating_overall` DESC (the "highest_rated" sort) and as the default tiebreak for "most_reviews". `tier_state` is read in a **separate, downstream** `vendor_profiles` query (l.1426) — *after* SQL has already ordered and paginated. So a FREE/VERIFIED-comment-blocked vendor with high hidden ratings is sorted to the top of "highest rated", then the card displays "new". The display is gated; the ordering is not. The spec gates the leaf prop and (in 2c) flags badges, but the same leak through `ORDER BY` is unaddressed and strictly worse than the badge case because it's the page's default ordering.

This is real, not hypothetical: marketplace surfacing is gated by `public_visibility`, **not** `tier_state` (l.996, l.1024 — `allowedVisibilities`), and `marketplaceSearchable: false` for FREE is **not yet enforced** (that's still-pending task #19, "name-reveal + searchability read tier_state"). So FREE vendors with `public_visibility='verified'` do appear and do get sorted by hidden stars today.

I confirmed `vendor_market_stats` (migration `20260607020000_vendor_market_stats_setnayan_first.sql`) does **not** expose `tier_state`, so you cannot gate the sort inside the existing view query without a view change.

**Minimal correct fix for the leak** — pick one:
- (a) **Re-sort in memory after enrichment.** The loop at l.1526 already has `caps`. After computing gated `rating`/`reviewCount` per vendor, re-apply the `highest_rated`/`most_reviews` ordering on the gated values within the page (and the default tiebreak). Cheap, no migration, keeps the view query for the cheap first-pass. Downside: re-sort is per-page (post-pagination), so a FREE vendor could still be *paginated in* by hidden stars even if re-sorted within the page — acceptable for V1 given the founder-only marketplace (memory: only 1 published vendor today), but note it.
- (b) **Add `tier_state` to the `vendor_market_stats` view** (one column at the tail — the migration explicitly documents the append-at-end constraint) and make the SQL `ORDER BY` use `CASE WHEN tier_state IN ('verified','pro','enterprise') THEN avg_rating_overall ELSE 0 END`. Correct at the SQL layer (fixes pagination too), but it's a migration + view change = small net-new DB work, and `tier_state` then leaks into a `security_invoker` view (acceptable — it's not PII).

Recommend (a) for V1 (no migration, matches the spec's "piggyback existing reads, no new queries" ethos) and flag (b) as the post-launch correctness upgrade. **Owner sign-off needed** on which — same judgment-call class as the spec's own point 2c (badges). Treat badges + sort as one decision: "should FREE vendors be ranked/badged by hidden stars?" If no, fix both at l.1526 in the same pass.

## Corrected / minimal spec delta (everything else in the spec stands as written)

Add to **Enforcement point 2**, new sub-step **2d (REQUIRED, was missing):**
> The marketplace orders by `avg_rating_overall`/`review_count` inside the `vendor_market_stats` view query (l.1156-1176), *before* `tier_state` is read (l.1426). Gating the card prop alone leaves FREE/VERIFIED-blocked vendors ranked by hidden stars while displaying "new". (Post-pagination re-sort is acceptable for the founder-only marketplace; a `tier_state`-aware view `ORDER BY` is the fuller fix — owner picks.) Fold this into the same decision as 2c (badges): one owner call on "FREE vendors ranked/badged by hidden stars — yes/no."

## RLS / privacy / searchability concerns

- **No new RLS exposure.** All three surfaces already use the `admin` service-role client and were already returning these reviews publicly; the gate only *removes* data from FREE/VERIFIED vendors' public display. It cannot widen exposure.

The review-comments gate is being built on a surface where the upstream tier-searchability gate isn't in place yet. This isn't a defect *in* this spec, but the review-sort leak (2d) and the searchability gap are best fixed together so you don't ship a half-gated marketplace. Surface to owner: **sequence task #19 (searchability) with or before this gate**, or at minimum fix the sort (2d) so the two land coherently.
- **No searchability regression introduced** by this gate itself.

## CORRECTED / MINIMAL SPEC

### SUB-GATE 1 — custom slug = PRO/ENT only → **SHIP (sound, ship-it)**

Enforcement point, reuse-the-probe, and downgrade-doesn't-error semantics are all correct. Apply with these refinements:

- **Take the spec's recommended Option (a):** fold `business_slug` into the *existing* `tierRow` select (`actions.ts:207-211` → `.select('tier_state, business_slug')`), derive `const caps = tierCaps(...)` once, set `portfolioMax = caps.portfolioPhotos`, and guard on `!caps.customWebsiteName && business_slug !== currentSlug` using `tierRow.business_slug` as `currentSlug`. This is one query (not the spec's Option-(b) third query) and avoids a redundant fetch. Keep the spec's "reject the *change*, never error on an unchanged save" logic verbatim — it correctly prevents a downgrade from blocking profile saves.
- **No new collision risk:** because the guard blocks any slug *change* for FREE/VERIFIED, the existing `business_slug` UNIQUE INDEX is never newly stressed. (Spec's "no uniqueness migration" note is wrong but harmless to the design.)
- **RLS:** both the read and the write are the vendor's own row via `supabase` (anon/auth client, RLS-scoped to `user_id`). No cross-vendor exposure. ✅
- **UI hint** (profile/page.tsx 194-202 + 441-448): advisory only, exactly as specced — thread `canCustomSlug = caps.customWebsiteName` into `loaderState`, destructure at line 300-301, `disabled={!canCustomSlug}` + "Pro feature" help on the slug input. Ship the server guard regardless of the UI.

### SUB-GATE 2 — basic-vs-custom microsite render = VERIFIED+ → **DEFER (net-new, but re-justify)**

The DEFER recommendation is **correct** — there is genuinely no basic-vs-custom *section-suppression* fork to amend; building one is a feature, not a gate. But the spec's *reason* ("FREE isn't public so this never fires") is **false** and must be replaced, or the owner will defer for the wrong reason and a real reachable-FREE-microsite case will slip through. Corrected framing for owner sign-off:

1. The microsite IS reachable by a `tier_state='free'` vendor (any vendor at `public_visibility ∈ {coming_soon, verified}` whose tier was never set). So a `website:'basic'` render path **would** fire — there's just no basic template to render.
2. The codebase **already** differentiates the microsite by tier via two *other* shipped gates — name-reveal (`resolveVendorDisplayName(isPaidTier)`, `nameMode`) and review visibility (`reviewStarsCounted` FREE=false / `reviewCommentsViewable` FREE,VERIFIED=false). So "tier-differentiated microsite" is not unprecedented; only the `caps.website` section-fork is missing. Owner must define what "basic" *shows* (logo + display-name + inquire only? no portfolio/packages/details?) before this is buildable.
3. **If owner wants the minimal scoped version now**, the spec's option-2 mechanics are correct (add `tier_state` to both selects 197/199, extend the fallback regex 206 to include `tier_state`, add the field to `PublicVendorRow` ~69-117, compute `caps` and wrap the four rich sections). **Required additions the spec missed:**
   - **Coordinate with pending task #19** ("name-reveal + searchability read tier_state"). #19 needs the *exact same* `tier_state` read into the microsite (today `resolveVendorDisplayName` is called with a non-tier `isPaidTier`; see vendors.ts:344-348 stale comment). Do the `tier_state` select-string + regex change **once**, shared by #19 and Sub-gate 2 — don't ship two PRs that both add `tier_state` to the same two select strings.
   - Wrapping the rich sections must **not** alter the name-reveal or review-visibility logic (those stay keyed to `nameMode`/review caps, not `website`).

# VERDICT: **needs-fix** (sound architecture, two factually-wrong load-bearing claims, one real bug in the fail-open path)

The enforcement point is **correct** and the architecture is sound, but the spec ships on a **false safety argument** and contains **one genuine fail-open bug**. All structural claims verified against `origin/main` @ `1c50c3e5`. This is legitimately net-new behavior (task #22 Phase C explicitly lists "radius" as pending), not a deferral.

## What verified TRUE (the spec got these right)
- `serviceRadiusKm` is defined-but-unread — exactly 5 refs, all declarations at lines 23/72/94/116/138 of `vendor-tier-caps.ts`. ✓
- Tier values FREE 0 / VERIFIED 20 / PRO 50 / ENT `Infinity`. ✓

## Real bug: fail-open is broken on probe failure (§2c)
The spec says: *"if the column is absent the select errors and `attrRows` is `undefined` → the `?? null` fallbacks make every vendor admit-unknown (fail-open). Safe."* **This is wrong for the radius dimension.** Trace it:

- Probe fails → `attrRows` undefined → `attrById` empty → `a = undefined` → `a?.tier` is `undefined`.
- `tierCaps(undefined)` does **not** return a neutral value — `asVendorTier(undefined)` defaults to **`'free'`**, so `tierCaps(undefined).serviceRadiusKm === 0`.
- `0 <= 0` is true → the `radiusKm <= 0` clause short-circuits → admit. So it *happens* to fail-open **only because FREE=0 skips the cut.**

For pax/venue_type the `?? null` genuinely fails open. For radius it fails open **by accident of FREE=0**, not by design. If the owner ever decides FREE should be radius-gated (e.g. FREE→20km), this "fail-open" silently becomes **fail-CLOSED on probe error** (unknown tier → treated as a finite radius → real vendors dropped on a transient query error). **Make fail-open explicit**: when `a === undefined` (row missing from the probe), admit unconditionally — don't route through `tierCaps`.

## Corrected minimal predicate (drop-in replacement for the §2c filter)
```ts
baseRows = baseRows.filter((r) => {
  const a = attrById.get(r.vendor_profile_id);
  const cap = a?.cap ?? null;
  const type = a?.type ?? null;
  const paxOk = pax === null || cap === null || cap >= pax;
  const typeOk = vType === null || type === null || type === vType;
  // Tier service-radius gate. EXPLICIT fail-open — admit when:
  //  · radius scope not requested, OR
  //  · the vendor row was missing from the tier probe (a === undefined →
  //    unknown tier; do NOT let tierCaps() coerce it to 'free'/0), OR
  //  · vendor has no HQ coords, OR
  //  · tier radius is non-finite (ENT) or ≤0 (FREE — not distance-scoped).
  // Only a finite >0 radius hard-cuts.
  const radiusKm = a ? tierCaps(a.tier).serviceRadiusKm : Infinity;
  const radiusOk =
    !needsRadiusScope ||
    a === undefined ||
    r.hq_latitude == null ||
    r.hq_longitude == null ||
    !Number.isFinite(radiusKm) ||
    radiusKm <= 0 ||
    haversineKm(args.anchorLat!, args.anchorLng!, r.hq_latitude, r.hq_longitude) <= radiusKm;
  return paxOk && typeOk && radiusOk;
});
```
